correctness.rationale: Direct incidence constraints force m arm-constant bits of even parity, giving code size 2^(m-1). For every received word, minimum distance equals sum of block minimum weights, plus cheapest arm flip if the unique preferred constants have odd parity, with ties eliminating parity cost. Counting ties/non-ties and the exact maximum local minimum yields the full polynomial. Independent brute force exhausts every received word at (4,2),(4,3),(4,4),(6,2), and formula checks 44 further grids; radii and deepest coefficients are proved for m>=4, both parities. Correct ML expression uses exactly one minimum-weight error representative per syndrome coset and assumes 0<=p<=1/2. Finite tests do not substitute for universal proof.

value.rationale: The recently introduced book-graph 2-sum family was characterized by minimum distance but not decoded-performance distribution. Every coefficient in this polynomial counts distinct syndrome cosets and determines the exact maximum-likelihood block-success probability for every BSC crossover, as well as sharp deepest-coset multiplicities and parity-sensitive covering radius. This is a complete infinite family decoding invariant with practical channel-metric interpretation, not merely generic code normalization, an arbitrary small case, or an unmotivated tiny improvement. No superiority of the family to other codes is claimed.
